arjuna_section: Price trades at ₹2,002.25, resting above the 50-day SMA of ₹1,921.90 and 200-day SMA of ₹1,909.61, preserving a broader bullish structure.
Short-term momentum has softened as price slipped below the 20-day SMA of ₹2,027.07 and the MACD at 22.69 trails its signal line at 32.40.
The stock is positioned in the upper half of its 52-week range (₹1,598.15 to ₹2,194.65) and holds comfortably inside the Bollinger Bands (₹1,969.13–₹2,085.01).
A 14-day ATR of ₹29.88 reflects moderate daily swings, but light volume at 0.34x the 50-day average indicates low institutional participation.
The broader bullish reading invalidates if price breaks below the 50-day VWAP of ₹1,963.77 and lower Bollinger Band of ₹1,969.13 on heavier volume.
chanakya_section: Bajaj Finserv trades at a P/E of ~31.2x-31.5x and P/B of ~4.1x against book value of ₹487.
EV/EBITDA and historical 5-year multiple ranges remain unknown for holding financial companies.
Peers like Aditya Birla Capital, Bajaj Holdings, and Cholamandalam benchmark the diversified financial services space.
Premium valuation is supported by strong operating growth across lending and insurance businesses, though multiples remain elevated.
hanuman_section: Q1 FY26 net profit grew 30% year-on-year to ₹2,789 crore on a 13% rise in total income to ₹35,451 crore.
Price of ₹2,002.25 trades comfortably above the 50-day SMA of ₹1,921.90 and 200-day SMA of ₹1,909.61.
The stock shows strong broader trend strength with an 11.22% three-month gain and 12 bullish strategies.
krishna_summary: Bajaj Finserv is a major Indian financial holding company operating large lending and insurance businesses.
Profits jumped 30% in Q1 FY26 to ₹2,789 crore, helping the stock gain 11.22% over three months.
The shares trade near ₹2,002.25, recovering above longer-term moving averages but facing mild short-term weakness.
Watch whether trading volume picks up and if the price can stay above the ₹1,980.95 floor.
levels: Immediate support rests at ₹1,980.95, with major lower support positioned at the 52-week low of ₹1,598.15.
Upward movement faces initial resistance at ₹2,119.30, followed by the 52-week high barrier at ₹2,194.65.
The 14-day average true range indicates a typical daily price movement of approximately ₹29.88.
Bollinger Bands span from ₹1,969.13 to ₹2,085.01, enclosing current price action near ₹2,002.25.
narada_section: Consolidated total income rose to ₹35,451 crore in Q1 compared to ₹31,480 crore in the year-ago period.
Consolidated net profit grew 30% year-on-year to ₹2,789 crore driven by steady lending and insurance performance.
Strong quarterly earnings supported a 3-month share price return of 11.22% with trend strength indicating bullish bias.

vibhishana_section: Short-term momentum has weakened as price fell below the 20-day SMA of ₹2,027.07 and MACD trails its signal line.
Trading volume is critically low at 0.34x its 50-day average, signaling lack of institutional buying support.
Valuation remains rich at a P/E of ~31.2x-31.5x and P/B of ~4.1x while one-year return remains negative at -1.47%.
vidura_section: Consolidated total income reached ₹35,451 crore in Q1 FY26, growing 13% YoY from ₹31,480 crore.
Consolidated Profit After Tax grew 30% YoY to ₹2,789 crore in Q1 FY26 versus ₹2,138 crore earlier.
Growth continues to be primarily led by key subsidiaries Bajaj Finance and insurance operations.
Consolidated ROE, ROCE, and standalone cash flow metrics remain unspecified in preliminary disclosures.
vyasa_section: Bajaj Finserv demonstrates strong quarterly earnings growth with net profit expanding 30% to ₹2,789 crore.
The broader technical trend remains positive above major long-term moving averages despite recent short-term consolidation.
Elevated valuation multiples and very low trading volume warrant caution against chasing current price levels.
Overall stance remains balanced as robust subsidiary fundamentals counter short-term technical and volume headwinds.
watch: A daily close below support at ₹1,980.95 or the 50-day VWAP of ₹1,963.77 signaling trend breakdown.
A breakout above resistance at ₹2,119.30 accompanied by volume exceeding the 50-day average.
Release of detailed financial disclosures clarifying consolidated ROE, ROCE, and standalone cash flows.
yudhishthira_section: Consolidated ROE, ROCE, and standalone cash flow figures are omitted from the filed preliminary disclosures.
Historical 5-year valuation multiples and EV/EBITDA metrics are completely unknown for peer contextualization.
Technical indicators conflict, showing a strong bullish trend bias alongside negative short-term momentum and mixed strategies.

glossary.52-week range: The highest and lowest the price has been over the past year.
glossary.ATR: How much the price typically moves in a single day. A measure of choppiness.
glossary.AUM: The total money investors have put into this fund.
glossary.Alpha: Return above what the benchmark delivered — the part credited to the manager.
glossary.Benchmark: The index the fund is trying to beat. Returns mean little without it.
glossary.Beta: How much the fund moves when the market moves. Above 1 swings harder than the market.
glossary.CAGR: The steady yearly rate that would have taken you from the starting value to today's.
glossary.EPS: The company's yearly profit divided across each share.
glossary.EV/EBITDA: The whole company's value compared to its operating earnings. Used to compare companies that carry different amounts of debt.
glossary.Exit Load: A fee charged if you sell your units before a set holding period.
glossary.Expense Ratio: The yearly fee the fund charges, as a percentage of your money. It is already taken out of the NAV you see.
glossary.MACD: Compares a short-term and a long-term price average. Crossing above suggests momentum is turning up, below that it is turning down.
glossary.Max Drawdown: The worst peak-to-bottom fall in the past. What a bad stretch has felt like.
glossary.NAV: The per-unit price of the fund, updated at the end of each trading day.
glossary.P/B: The price compared to what the company's assets are worth on paper.
glossary.P/E: Investors are paying this many rupees for every ₹1 the company earns in a year. High can mean expected growth, or an expensive price — it depends on the company.
glossary.ROCE: How well the company turns all its capital — including borrowed money — into profit.
glossary.ROE: How much profit the company makes from the money shareholders put in. Higher is better.
glossary.RSI: A 0-100 momentum gauge. Above 70 means the price has run up fast; below 30 means it has fallen fast. Neither is a buy or sell signal on its own.
glossary.Sharpe Ratio: Return earned per unit of bumpiness. Higher means a smoother ride for the same result.
